canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across papers, the dominant framing is direct source-to-target text conversion: a model generates a target-language sentence or text from a source-language sentence or text. Success is usually described as semantic equivalence or meaning preservation, and some definitions add fluency, adequacy, or natural sentence structure. A smaller line of work treats it as both a held-in and a generation task, or elicits it with an explicit prompt template that asks the model to translate from a named source language to a named target language.

Variants. A recurring variant is sentence-level translation, often bidirectional or multilingual, including low-resource settings and English-to-X or X-to-English directions. Papers also study document, paragraph, and pseudo-document translation, plus context-sensitive subproblems such as pronoun, proper noun, and context-dependent translation. Smaller lines of work examine zero-shot, in-context, dictionary-based, self-translation, monotonic and concise simultaneous translation, and domain-specific forms such as legal, finance, multi-domain, or cross-cultural translation. Modality- or format-specific variants include text-in-image, document-image plain-text, spoken-only IPA, Braille-to-text, lyrics, code-switched, gender-neutral or gendered, classical Chinese and poetry, and synthetic single-hop or multi-hop translation; one paper claims a causal relationship from chain of thought to machine translation because multi-hop translation accuracy approaches 0% when CoT is disabled.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link it to 20 measurement instruments. The most frequently linked are FLORES-200, FLORES, Flores-101, WMT16, and IWSLT 2017; the remaining instruments are other translation benchmarks, corpora, and evaluator setups. Elicitation is usually direct source-to-target prompting or seq2seq translation evaluation, and scoring is commonly reported with BLEU or SacreBLEU, with some papers also using BLEURT, XComet-XL, task-specific accuracy measures such as APT, or fine-grained quality annotations and LLM judging.

What it is taken as evidence of. Across the 5 linked constructs, the most recurrent construct link is cross-lingual generalization: one paper explicitly treats cross-lingual generalization as measured by machine translation. The construct links otherwise vary: one paper claims a causal relationship from cross-lingual alignment to machine translation, another claims a causal relationship from cross-lingual generalization to machine translation, machine translation is reported to correlate with translation quality, and it is related to naturalness and stereotyping. Papers therefore do not converge on a single construct framing beyond the recurring link to cross-lingual generalization.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, the dominant framing is direct source-to-target text conversion: a model generates a target-language sentence or text from a source-language sentence or text. Success is usually described as semantic equivalence or meaning preservation, and some definitions add fluency, adequacy, or natural sentence structure. A smaller line of work treats it as both a held-in and a generation task, or elicits it with an explicit prompt template that asks the model to translate from a named source language to a named target language.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: A recurring variant is sentence-level translation, often bidirectional or multilingual, including low-resource settings and English-to-X or X-to-English directions. Papers also study document, paragraph, and pseudo-document translation, plus context-sensitive subproblems such as pronoun, proper noun, and context-dependent translation. Smaller lines of work examine zero-shot, in-context, dictionary-based, self-translation, monotonic and concise simultaneous translation, and domain-specific forms such as legal, finance, multi-domain, or cross-cultural translation. Modality- or format-specific variants include text-in-image, document-image plain-text, spoken-only IPA, Braille-to-text, lyrics, code-switched, gender-neutral or gendered, classical Chinese and poetry, and synthetic single-hop or multi-hop translation; one paper claims a causal relationship from chain of thought to machine translation because multi-hop translation accuracy approaches 0% when CoT is disabled.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link it to 20 measurement instruments. The most frequently linked are FLORES-200, FLORES, Flores-101, WMT16, and IWSLT 2017; the remaining instruments are other translation benchmarks, corpora, and evaluator setups. Elicitation is usually direct source-to-target prompting or seq2seq translation evaluation, and scoring is commonly reported with BLEU or SacreBLEU, with some papers also using BLEURT, XComet-XL, task-specific accuracy measures such as APT, or fine-grained quality annotations and LLM judging.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Across the 5 linked constructs, the most recurrent construct link is cross-lingual generalization: one paper explicitly treats cross-lingual generalization as measured by machine translation. The construct links otherwise vary: one paper claims a causal relationship from cross-lingual alignment to machine translation, another claims a causal relationship from cross-lingual generalization to machine translation, machine translation is reported to correlate with translation quality, and it is related to naturalness and stereotyping. Papers therefore do not converge on a single construct framing beyond the recurring link to cross-lingual generalization.
